summary: @servicetitan/standalone-ui preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's npm preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun standalone runtime from GitHub releases (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`), unpacks it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')],...)` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line Bun-CJS bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with a shuffled string-array decoder (`function WV8StW(...) {...MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift()); return MmgoCP }`), hex-suffixed variable names, and no readable identifiers. Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time solely to execute an opaque, heavily obfuscated bundle is not the behavior of a React component library and matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern — the Bun execution deliberately routes the payload outside Node's visibility. The manifest declares `name: "@servicetitan/standalone-ui"` under the public `@servicetitan` scope with an empty `author` field and a description referencing ServiceTitan's internal `standalone-fe` repo, consistent with a dependency-confusion package intended to be resolved in place of an internal ServiceTitan artifact. Installing this package causes attacker-controlled code to execute automatically on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
